items.title: Delaware Academy removed from Section 4 football final over player eligibility; Middletown drops appeal ahead of Section 9 final
items.summary:
The Delaware Academy football team has been removed from the Section 4 Class AA playoffs for the use of an ineligible player in its sectional semifinal game. (Jim Franco/Times Union)

Another sectional football championship game in New York State has been thrown into chaos as a result of a ruling over player eligibility.

Meanwhile, a team that was previously forced to forfeit its spot in a championship game has dropped its appeal after heading to court seeking emergency relief to have its berth in a title game restored.

Thursday night, Delaware Academy announced that it had been forced to forfeit its Section 4 Class D semifinal win over Deposit/Hancock from this past weekend, removing the state's No. 2-ranked Class D team from its spot in a sectional final this weekend.

In a letter posted to the district's Facebook page , Delaware Academy Central School District at Delhi Superintendent Carey Shultz wrote that Section 4 had ruled the Bulldogs must forfeit their semifinal win and the remainder of their 2026 season "due to a sectional eligibility rule we were unaware of."

In the letter, Shultz said that the ruling came in the wake of a similar issue that occurred elsewhere in the state. items.title: Clay Holmes Free Agency: Five Landing Spots For The Starter
items.summary:
Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Clay Holmes is back on the market, and the deal looks different this time. The former Yankees closer has successfully turned himself into a starting pitcher. After throwing 101 1/3 innings for the Chicago Cubs and New York Mets, he turned down his $12 million player option for 2027. A fractured right fibula stopped his season in May, but he returned in August to make nine starts for Chicago, according to Just Baseball . Beyond the top-tier names on the market, franchises now view him as a reliable rotation choice.

His numbers show a pitcher who limits damage rather than striking out everyone. Holmes posted a 3.29 ERA last season with a 3.63 FIP and a 1.19 WHIP. He gave up only six home runs in 101 1/3 innings. The 33-year-old relies on a sinker that accounts for nearly half his pitches. Just Baseball states that he induced groundballs on 60.8% of batted balls during the previous season. This skill set helps him limit hard contact even when his 18.6% strikeout rate stays low.

The Mets Return to the Fold Just Baseball predicts Holmes will sign a three-year, $54 million deal with the New York Mets. That works out to an $18 million annual average value. Prior to 2025, he inked a three-year, $38 million deal with the Mets following years spent mostly in relief. New York gave him the chance to start again, a role he had not held regularly since his minor league days. He answered with 165 2/3 innings, a career high, alongside a 3.53 ERA in 31 starts. The Mets know his stuff, and they know he can handle the innings.

items.title: Annika 2026: Three players share lead after 36 holes
items.summary:
BELLEAIR, Fla. — Hye-Jin Choi opened with two bogeys, made up ground with a 15-foot eagle putt late and finished with a 3-under 67 Friday that gave her a three-way share of the lead at The Annika and another chance to win for the first time in 127 tries on the LPGA Tour.

It was far more effective than the bogey-free round of Nelly Korda, the No. 1 player who could only laugh at her clean card because it was cleaner than she would have preferred — 15 straight pars, one birdie, two closing pars for a 69.

That left Korda four shots behind going into the week at Pelican Golf Club, where a victory would make the 28-year-old American eligible for the LPGA Hall of Fame.

“I had a lot of chances,” said Korda, competing for the first time in two months. “But you can just tell that from yesterday morning to today afternoon with the wind, that’s what the defense of this golf course is. It’s as fast as Bermuda as I’ve putted on throughout my career.”

It wasn’t a problem for Solheim Cup star Carlota Ciganda , who birdied her last four holes for a 63 to join Choi and Lindy Duncan (66) atop the leaderboard at 12-under 128.

The Japanese duo of Mao Saigo (65) and Minami Katsu (69) were two shots behind.

Choi has been an LPGA member for five years and it has been a curious chase for that first LPGA victory, particularly since she was 17 when she had a late lead in the 2017 U.S. Women’s Open and wound up as a runner-up.

She also had two good chances at winning during the recent Asia swing, where she was runner-up in Shanghai and South Korea.

items.title: A sudden FAA ground stop strands teams and throws the sports weekend into chaos
items.summary:
The Federal Aviation Administration's decision to ground all flights nationwide Friday threw the sports world into chaos, leaving NBA, NHL and college teams stranded as they tried to reach their destinations, and NFL teams were left to wonder whether the issue would be resolved in time for them to travel to their games this weekend.

The FAA issued a notice that said the ground stop was “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety." 

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy later said there was a communications issue affecting the 22 regional air traffic control centers that direct planes en route between airports nationwide, and that FAA technicians were investigating.

“There’s no reason to be concerned about your loved ones if they’re flying,” Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said.

Most college football teams playing Saturday travel the day before their game, and the stoppage left many schools — including No. 2 Utah, eighth-ranked Texas and No. 9 Tennessee — at a standstill as they departed for road games. The Utes play at No. 22 Arizona, the Longhorns visit No. 24 LSU and the Vols are traveling to Texas A&M in three of the bigger games of the weekend. 

In the case of the Longhorns, they posted on social media a short video of them boarding their plane before the stoppage. If they end up taking a bus to Baton Rouge, the trip for the 6:30 p.m. CT kickoff Saturday takes about seven hours.

items.title: Tigers 'Showing Interest' In Cubs Free Agent Who Gives Up A Ton Of Home Runs
items.summary: Free agent pitcher Shota Imanaga The Detroit Tigers could use some more pitching, and according to MLB Network's Jon Morosi , they are "showing interest" in Shota Imanaga. The Tigers traded away Tarik Skubal and Casey Mize at the trade deadline and Jack Flaherty is a free agent. The rotation will need some new arms, and Imanaga is an interesting case. He is not one of the top arms on the market, but he does have a 3.45 ERA in 86 career starts with the Chicago Cubs. He had a 3.77 ERA last season and struck out 174 batters. Michael King and Freddy Peralta seem like better options, and the Tigers will surely check in on them as well. While Imanaga does have an All-Star nod, he has one fatal flaw. He gives up a ton of home runs. He gave up 35 homers last season and 31 in 2025. Even during his All-Star season, he gave up 27 home runs. He has been top five in home runs allowed in each of his seasons as a big leaguer, and was second last season. On a positive note, he does not walk a ton of batters. He ranked in the 95th percentile for walk rate last season. Imanaga could perform better in Comerica Park. It is a tougher venue to hit home runs in than Wrigley Field, which could help solve some of his woes. More MLB: Cubs Superstar Wins 2026 NL MVP After Historic Season

Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers (11-2) currently lead the Western Conference standings, but they face multiple injuries ahead of Sunday’s game against the Phoenix Suns (5-6). Fortunately, they’ve avoided any long-term setbacks , but Lakers fans are still concerned about the team’s current state.

That’s why, on Friday, head coach JJ Redick provided clarity in a chat with the media, revealing the latest development with each of the four injured Lakers guards: Austin Reaves , Luka Doncic , Collin Sexton , and Quentin Grimes .

“Luka is fine,” said Redick on Friday, via Mark Medina . “The expectation would be that he’s available. AR is based on his physical evaluation and how he was feeling yesterday. We opted against imaging; he’ll be day-to-day. We’ll have him on the report tomorrow at 5:00. Collin is in the same boat. Concussion’s been ruled out; he ended up getting stitches, and he’ll be day-to-day. And then Q [Quentin Grimes] was able to do the live part of the stay-ready game.” 

Plenty of NBA teams have been plagued by injuries this season, and the Lakers are no exception. Since opening night, they’ve had various players in and out of the lineup, but it hasn’t made much of a difference. Thanks to Redick’s coaching, a loaded roster, and heroics from Luka (averaging 38.6 points, 7.5 rebounds, 7.6 assists, 2.0 steals, and 0.7 blocks per game on 48.9% shooting), they’ve been a dominant force in the West, but things could always take a turn for the worse.

items.title: Florida basketball’s Boogie Fland out against Merrimack
items.summary:
Florida basketball will be without starting point guard Boogie Fland in the Gators’ home game against Merrimack on Friday, Nov. 13.

Sophomore Alex Lloyd will earn the start in Fland’s place, according to a team spokesperson.

Fland is dealing with a shoulder injury that he sustained in the Gators’ 81-72 win over Florida State earlier in the week. The junior is expected to be available next week when UF travels to Las Vegas to compete in the Players Era Tournament.

Fland previously missed the Gators’ exhibition game against Stetson due to an illness. In that matchup, Urban Klavzar started and scored 24 points.

Through three games, Fland has averaged 10 points and three rebounds per game.

items.title: France cling on for furious victory against South Africa after Dupont sizzles
items.summary:
• France 21-19 South Africa

  • Scrum-half key in thriller full of twists and turns

Friday night at the Stade de France may just be the best show in sport. The French had laid on a full Cecil B DeMille production: fireworks, flamethrowers, floodlights, a multicoloured drone show involving a three-storey-tall cockerel that then reassembled itself into a beating red, blue and white heart before transforming into a vast tricolore along with 150 dancers carrying LEDs who performed to an ear-splitting choral rendition of Madonna’s Like a Prayer. Astonishingly enough, what came after actually lived up to it.

It had twists and turns, a scattering of superb performances from some of the finest players in the game, a fistful of red and yellow cards, fantastic free-wheeling tries and several agonisingly intense stretches of scrummaging and defence, a clutch of hugely controversial decisions by both coaches and the referee, and one crucial missed conversion. At the end of it all, somehow, France had won by two points, 21-19, in their first victory against the Springboks at their national stadium in 21 years.

items.title: Cummins stands firm on ball tampering to leave Australian cricket back where it started | Geoff Lemon
items.summary:
The Test captain kept his promise to answer all questions at a press conference that made his position clear and filled some but not all gaps

Our coverage on Thursday said that Pat Cummins needed to front up, and nobody can fairly say that he didn’t. It was a proper ’til-they-drop affair from Australia’s cricket captain, an hour and eight minutes at a press conference podium taking questions about the 2018 ball-tampering episode until every journalist present ran out of steam. You might have expected some partial concession to teammate Usman Khawaja’s depiction of endemic cheating, but Cummins was firm that this did not reflect the life he’d known. Once more with feeling, but more importantly with detail.

Media accounts will now depict this as Cummins and Khawaja at war, because a falling-out among friends is a juicy story to fatten up and serve for gluttony. It isn’t fair, because both have emphasised the importance of their friendship, strained as it must now be. As two thoughtful people with shared history, they have a better chance than most to find a way through.

items.title: NFL quarterbacks are under more pressure than ever from rushers. Why?
items.summary:
Despite all the advantages offenses have secured over the years, defenses are better at pressuring the QB than any other time in recent history

The Baltimore Ravens are preparing to start their fourth quarterback this year, Jacoby Brissett, against the beleaguered Los Angeles Chargers on Monday, because of injuries to Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley and Joe Fagnano. That puts them dangerously close to the NFL record of five within a single season (a record shared by the 1984 Bears and 2023 Browns when excluding the 1987 strike season).

Jackson, Huntley and Fagnano were all injured after taking hits in games. And if it seems like quarterbacks are taking punishment more often this year, your eyes aren’t deceiving you. Through nine weeks, quarterbacks have been hit on 15.1% of their dropbacks, the most we’ve seen since 2006, when hits were first logged in official box scores.

Magnus Carlsen makes a very rare appearance in an open tournament on 5-6 December when the Norwegian, who has topped the world rankings for 15 successive years, competes in the 10-round Super Rapid at the XTX Markets London Classic. The venue is the Novotel West at Hammersmith and the time limit is 15 minutes per player for the entire game, plus a 10 seconds increment for each move.

In 2025, 267 players entered the Super Rapid. On Monday, when Carlsen’s participation was announced, the entry doubled in just 12 hours and is now close to 400. The capacity is 500 and Alex Holowczak, the chief arbiter, expects that figure to be reached this weekend or early next week. items.title: The beautiful game: revived art prize gives football its creative due once more | Emma John
items.summary:
Football and the art world have long remained distant but the breadth of entries for this year’s award reveals a healthy revival

It may be the Beautiful Game, but in its early decades football was a rare subject for artists. The Italian Futurist Umberto Boccioni whirled an athlete’s body into a vortex of movement in his 1913 painting Dynamism of a Soccer Player. You can see one of the earliest fine art depictions of a match – a smoggy, factory-adjactent scene called Any Wintry Afternoon in England – at the Manchester Art Gallery. If 1930s abstraction is more your thing, you can enjoy decoding the geometric shapes in Kazimir Malevich’s Painterly Realism of a Football Player – Color Masses in the 4th Dimension. I’m guessing the small green pea shape is a ball.

These, in any case, were exceptions. In 1953 the Football Association launched an art prize, backed by the newly formed Arts Council: the winning works included Going To The Match by LS Lowry, with its crowds flocking to Bolton Wanderers’ then home ground, Burnden Park. An exhibition of the submissions, Football and The Fine Arts, toured the country and the FA secretary, Sir Stanley Rous, said he hoped it would finally break the barrier between those two worlds.
